Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, patchy, fluffy airspace opacities (consolidations) with visible air bronchograms, particularly in the mid-to-lower lung zones. This radiological pattern of non-segmental, migrating, or persistent consolidation is highly characteristic of Bronchus-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (BALT) lymphoma (also known as MALT lymphoma), which often presents as multifocal consolidations that can mimic pneumonia but persist over time. While Organizing Pneumonia (OP) has a similar appearance, BALT lymphoma is a classic "mimic" frequently tested with this specific presentation of bilateral consolidations without significant lymphadenopathy or cavitation.
